tickets.title: Reconcile the fiscal graph artifact contract
tickets.goal: Extend and reconcile WAVE-130 into one versioned contract for StateCivics fiscal graph projections, including entity and relationship identity, exact source spans and citations, ACL and lifecycle state, derivation-run identity, and withdrawal/version semantics without creating a competing contract.
tickets.acceptance: WAVE-130 is updated in place and docs/CELL_GRAPH_PROFILES.md gains one fiscal v1 contract. The contract defines fiscal-specific file, node, edge, artifact, publication, evidence-class, ACL, citation, derivation-run, replacement, and withdrawal fields; requires one derivation_run_id per artifact; requires every projected assertion to bind a current ExAIS fiscal document carrying its source revision and exact non-null StateCivics source span; normalizes source revision hashes to lowercase hex; treats upstream eligibility fields as trusted exporter assertions that ExAIS validates structurally but cannot independently prove; and explicitly leaves Grant, court, and Topeka contracts unchanged. It defines type-specific eligibility: ontology dimensions require publication_status=published, resolution_status=resolved, lifecycle_status=active, and a source span; positive AccountCrosswalk edges require a positive relationship, status=published, publication_allowed=true, completed review evidence, an effective period, source references, and current revision identity. A published not_same decision is retained upstream as a valid negative decision but never emitted as a positive expansion edge; unknown, candidate, in_review, rejected, superseded, unresolved, ambiguous, or publication-disallowed crosswalks cannot create positive edges. Current ticket states are dependency signals only. Real activation depends on a dated inspection of actual candidate export rows and fields, not ticket status.

tickets.title: Add a bounded curated fiscal projection path
tickets.goal: Define the fixture-safe and production-ready projection/derivation path that consumes reviewed StateCivics fiscal relationships, reuses the existing PostgreSQL graph loader and custody checks, and supports bounded one-hop expansion without ingesting transaction rows as narrative documents.
tickets.acceptance: A fiscal validator and expander accept a deterministic JSONL projection under the existing VectorStoreGraphLoadRequest and PostgreSQL graph tables. The first implementable MVP preserves WAVE-130's fiscal ontology use case with fiscal_document, agency, fund, budget_unit, program, and account nodes and only source-backed describes_dimension and parent_dimension relations. It can be built and tested against fixtures now; real loading requires a new explicit StateCivics structured relationship export with stable source-revision/document/span bindings because the current narrative retrieval exporter exports documents, not canonical relationships. Ontology eligibility uses publication_status=published, resolution_status=resolved, lifecycle_status=active and a non-null source span. Account crosswalk support is additive only when upstream exports it: positive edges require status=published, publication_allowed=true, completed review evidence, effective period, source refs, current revision, and relationship in same_account, payment_reports_against_account, program_contains_account, alias_of, predecessor_of, or successor_of. not_same is a negative assertion and cannot expand positively; unknown, unresolved, candidate, ambiguous, disallowed, rejected, or superseded records cannot create a positive edge. The broader exact bill-version to appropriation/account to reviewed crosswalk to payment/outcome chain remains the product direction, but bill-version/action edges require an explicit cited upstream export and payment, observation, and impact edges remain fixture-only until their own structured cited export exists. Raw transactions never become narrative documents, amounts are never reconstructed by summing search hits, and embeddings never establish joins. Validation also enforces one derivation run, current-document joins, ACL scope, lowercase hashes, no dangling nodes, 1..20 citations per edge, fewer than 10,000 nodes and 20,000 edges, and one-hop expansion capped at 10.
